prior_approach.content: Prior work used intersystem-crossing-based optical-spin interfaces in known ODMR systems such as NV, SiC defects, and VB in hBN.
prior_approach.evidence_span: These systems, including the NV defect in diamond, rely on spin-dependent intersys- tem crossings between the ground and excited states [11].

prior_approach.content: Recent studies in hBN, GaN, and β-GeS2 reported S=1/2-like ODMR signatures attributed to defect-pair charge transfer.
prior_approach.evidence_span: More recently, a series of observations in hBN [12–19], gallium nitride (GaN) [20], and β-germanium disulphide (β-GeS2) [21, 22] have identified an ODMR signature akin to a S = 1/2 resonance, which is generally con- sidered to be inconsistent with the intersystem cross- ing optical-spin interface and may instead be better ex- plained by spin dependent charge transfer between defect pairs [18].

prior_approach.content: Prior ODMR work distinguished two optical-spin-interface mechanisms: established ODMR systems such as NV centers in diamond, SiC defects, and VB defects in hBN were understood via spin-dependent intersystem crossing, whereas more recent S=1/2-like ODMR reports in hBN, GaN, and β-GeS2 were attributed instead to spin-dependent charge transfer between defect pairs; in hBN, such spin-pair ODMR was noted to be ubiquitous over a wide range of laser excitation wavelengths.
evidence_spans: These systems, including the NV defect in diamond, rely on spin-dependent intersys- tem crossings between the ground and excited states [11].

More recently, a series of observations in hBN [12–19], gallium nitride (GaN) [20], and β-germanium disulphide (β-GeS2) [21, 22] have identified an ODMR signature akin to a S = 1/2 resonance, which is generally con- sidered to be inconsistent with the intersystem cross- ing optical-spin interface and may instead be better ex- plained by spin dependent charge transfer between defect pairs [18].
A characteristic feature for the optical spin defect pairs in hBN is the ubiquity of the ODMR signal under a wide range of different wavelengths of laser excitation [33].

prior_approach.content: Prior hBN studies had already reported similar ODMR signatures and a broad range of comparable photodynamic values; hBN nanopowder had also been used previously as a reference sample for spin-pair ODMR.
evidence_spans: Overall these values appear consistent with the broad range previously measured in hBN [18].
The ODMR signature exhibits the same features previously observed in hBN
In addition to the cBN samples we also used a hBN nanopowder purchased in 2017 from Graphene Super- market (BN Ultrafine Powder) as a reference for spin pair ODMR (see ref. [15]).

prior_approach.content: Prior approaches in scanning magnetometry commonly used NV defects in diamond, and in a simple implementation the quantum-sensor-containing particle is attached to an AFM tip.
evidence_spans: The simplest imple- mentation of this technique involves attaching a parti- cle embedded with quantum sensors on to an AFM tip.
While NV defects in diamond are commonly used for this purpose

prior_approach.content: Prior analysis approaches fit Rabi oscillations using a previously reported phenomenological model, including a constrained version in which the beat frequency was set equal to the Rabi frequency.
evidence_spans: We fit the Rabi oscillations with the following phenomenologi- cal model[15]
Rabi measurements taken over a range of MW powers fit with a phenomenological model where the beat frequency is constrained to the Rabi frequency.

prior_approach.content: An alternative prior fitting approach modeled the Rabi measurements with unconstrained Rabi frequency components.
evidence_spans: Rabi measurement fit with unconstrained Rabi frequency compo- nents.

prior_limitation.content: Prior work on ODMR could not cleanly attribute contrast variations to excitation wavelength because uncontrolled factors such as differences in incident power density were not controlled.
evidence_spans: variations in the ODMR contrast cannot be attributed specifically to changes in excitation wavelength and may instead be the result of uncontrolled parameters, for example differences in the incident power density

prior_limitation.content: Diamond NV-based scanning magnetometry has practical limitations: it requires precise alignment with an external bias field due to the anisotropy of the S = 1 ground state, and the currently used particle size would inhibit the spatial resolution of scanning magnetometry images.
evidence_spans: this system requires precise alignment with an external bias field due to the inherent anisotropy of the S = 1 ground state [37].
however, the size of the particle currently would inhibit the spa- tial resolution of a scanning magnetometry image.

prior_limitation.content: At present, cBN defects are less attractive than NV centers for sensing because their low ODMR contrast and short coherence time give inferior sensitivity, and their spin/optical properties lack distinctive features (such as hyperfine structure in ODMR or zero-phonon lines) that would clearly distinguish them from hBN.
evidence_spans: Furthermore, the low ODMR contrast and short coherence time lead to an inferior sensitivity to the NV defect
Without significant defining features in the spin and optical properties (e.g. hyperfine features in ODMR or zero-phonon lines) to distinguish the samples from hBN

rejected_alternative.content: The authors rejected using post-treated cBN samples and instead studied untreated commercial samples as received, without irradiation, implantation, or thermal annealing.
evidence_spans: All samples were studied 6 as recieved without additional treatment (e.g. no irradi- ation, implantation, or thermal annealing).

rejected_alternative.content: Rather than studying all particle sizes/samples, the authors focused on 165 nm cBN particles because they provide a more uniform source of PL and ODMR.
evidence_spans: For these measurements, we focus on only the 165 nm cBN particles, as they are a more uniform source of PL and ODMR.

inspiration_source.content: Previously discovered optical spin defect pairs in hBN, specifically the optical-spin interface based on charge transfer between such defect pairs, served as the inspiration/source for the interpretation.
evidence_spans: This is con- sistent with the optical-spin interface based on charge transfer between optical spin defect pairs previously dis- covered in hBN

causal_claim.content: Increasing microwave power causes the Rabi frequency to increase linearly on the plotted scale, and at higher powers a secondary oscillation emerges.
evidence_spans: the Rabi frequency increases linearly when plotted against a logarithmically increasing MW power
Additionally, a secondary oscillation also emerges at higher powers.

causal_claim.content: Longer dark periods lead to PL recovery.
evidence_spans: a clear recovery of the PL, with a 1/e time Trec ≈3 ms as the system is left in the dark for longer periods

causal_claim.content: The spin-1/2-like weakly coupled spin-pair nature in cBN enables isotropic sensing and simplifies scanning magnetometer design.
evidence_spans: the spin- 1/2-like nature of the weakly coupled spin pair system in cBN enables isotropic sensing and can thus simplify the experimental design of the scanning magnetometer [38]

causal_claim.content: Spin and photodynamic measurements allowed the authors to link the ODMR features to multiple emitters and a defect-pair charge-transfer mechanism.
evidence_spans: Performing a series of spin and photodynamic measurements, we were able to associate these features with a defect ensemble containing multiple different op- tical emitters where ODMR arises from a charge trans- fer mechanism involving defect pairs.

causal_claim.content: Separating the optical-spin interface from host-specific properties via a charge-transfer mechanism broadens access to ODMR-active defects across a wider array of materials.
evidence_spans: In this sense, the charge transfer mechanism has the potential to pro- vide access to ODMR active defects in a wider array of materials than previously considered.
and corroborates evidence from other works indicating such defect pair systems may be accessi- ble in a diverse range of materials.

causal_claim.content: Investigating single emitters could reveal defect structure through zero-phonon lines or hyperfine ODMR features, aiding ab initio calculations, and may uncover more exotic spin-complex systems similar to those found in hBN.
evidence_spans: which could lead to better insight into the defect structure through zero-phonon lines or hyper- fine features in the ODMR to aid in ab initio calculations.
Such studies may also reveal more exotic systems, such as recently identified spin complexes observed in hBN from the same class of defects [17, 19].

causal_claim.content: Confirmation of the Ω1 = 2Ω2 relation supports the conclusion that the defect ensemble consists of weakly coupled spin pairs.
evidence_spans: Confirming the Ω1 = 2Ω2 relationship strongly suggests the defect ensemble is composed of weakly coupled spin pairs.

mechanism_principle.content: The charge-transfer ODMR mechanism is less dependent on specific host/defect properties, relaxing requirements for ODMR occurrence.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: An interesting aspect of the charge transfer mechanism is the optical-spin interface is effectively sep- arate from the specific material and defect properties, which significantly relaxes the conditions under which these systems may arise, i.e. the ODMR mechanism is agnostic to the host material

mechanism_principle.content: The sharp lower-intensity features are assigned to cBN Raman lines and the broad peak to ensemble photoluminescence from optical emitters.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The latter are associated with the cBN Raman lines (see SI) while we attribute the main broad peak to PL from an ensemble of optical emit- ters [34].

mechanism_principle.content: Excitation-wavelength ubiquity is explained by interchangeability of the optical defect in the defect-pair model, allowing multiple emitters to participate.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This feature arises due to the interchangeability of the optical defect component in the optical spin defect pair model, allowing for multiple different optical emitters (e.g. with distinct absorption and emission spectra)

mechanism_principle.content: The broad PL is interpreted as a distribution of zero-phonon lines, implying multiple distinct optical emitters in the ensemble.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This can be interpreted as the defect ensem- ble containing a distribution of zero-phonon lines which suggests the ensemble contains multiple distinct optical emitters

mechanism_principle.content: The shared 700 nm PL peak in 2 µm particles suggests both lasers excite the same subset of emitters.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: which instead suggests these lasers are exciting the same subset of emitters within the ensemble

mechanism_principle.content: The 2:1 frequency relation is expected for a weakly coupled spin pair system.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: as expected from a weakly coupled spin pair system

mechanism_principle.content: The asymmetric envelope is consistent with a metastable spin-pair configuration undergoing spin-dependent recombination to the ground state.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: consistent with a metastable configuration of the spin pair which experiences spin de- pendent recombination back to its ground state

mechanism_principle.content: The PL decay behavior indicates optical pumping into a dark metastable state.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: which suggests opti- cal pumping into a dark metastable state

mechanism_principle.content: The recovery indicates the optical state is restored as the metastable state decays in the dark.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: indicating a recovery of the optical state as the metastable state de- cays

mechanism_principle.content: In the model, optical excitation can cause spin-dependent charge transfer to a remote defect, separating two electrons into a weakly coupled spin pair.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: When the system is in the ground state, two electrons are co-localised on the optical defect and upon optical excitation, a spin depen- dent charge transfer to the remote defect can occur which separates the two electrons forming the weakly coupled spin pair.

mechanism_principle.content: Quantum sensing works by driving transitions between T± and ST0 states and reading out via spin-dependent recombination.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Quantum sensing is enabled by driving be- tween the T± and ST0 states of the weakly coupled spin pair which can then be optically read out after spin de- pendent recombination.

mechanism_principle.content: Consistency between hBN and cBN despite structural differences suggests the charge-transfer optical spin defect-pair model is independent of crystal phase.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Noting the struc- tural differences between hBN and cBN, the consistency of the ODMR features implies the optical spin defect pair model based on the charge transfer mechanism is agnos- tic to crystal phase

mechanism_principle.content: Other common quantum-sensor hosts cannot operate in these conditions because they burn or oxidize in air at high temperature.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: (which all burn or oxidise in air at elevated temperatures).

hypothesis_statement.content: Testing a different crystal phase can probe whether the same charge-transfer ODMR mechanism applies beyond hBN.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: A simple way of exploring this possibility is to consider a different crystal phase of a material in which the charge transfer mecha- nism has already been observed. Here we consider cubic boron nitride (cBN)

hypothesis_statement.content: The work tests whether indicators of the optical-spin defect-pair and charge-transfer ODMR mechanism are present in cBN.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Specifically, we inves- tigate characteristic spin and optical properties which are indicators of the optical-spin defect pair model and the underlying charge transfer mechanism for ODMR

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors test whether cBN shows behavior similar to previously observed ODMR signatures.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To test whether cBN exhibits similar behaviour

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors aim to confirm that the observed emitters participate in the optical spin defect pair.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We next confirm the observed emitters contribute to the optical spin defect pair by performing ODMR mea- surements using the different excitation lasers

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors probe spin and photodynamics to verify the charge-transfer mechanism of the optical spin defect pair model.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To verify the optical spin defect pair model we now probe the charge transfer mechanism by considering the spin and photodynamics of the cBN defect ensembles.

hypothesis_statement.content: The optically created metastable state is proposed to be the weakly coupled spin pair that recombines in the dark.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: the photodynamic behaviour suggests the optically cre- ated metastable state is the weakly coupled spin pair which undergoes recombination in the dark

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors investigate whether cBN optical spin defect pairs are feasible for micro- and nanoscale sensing.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Finally, we now explore the feasibility of micro and nanoscale sensing applications using cBN based optical spin defect pairs by isolating single particles from the 2 µm and 165 nm samples.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors test whether cBN particles are viable for scanning magnetometry.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In order to establish the viability of using cBN particles for this pur- pose, we measure ODMR from a defect ensemble in a sin- gle 2 µm particle [Fig. 4(h)].

hypothesis_statement.content: The beat frequency in the Rabi oscillations is interpreted as evidence of a weakly coupled spin-pair system.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Here we rationalise our interpretation of the beat fre- quency in the Rabi oscillations as evidence for a weakly coupled spin pair system

evidence_result.content: The study finds cBN ensemble ODMR consistent with prior hBN ensemble measurements.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In this work, we study ODMR signatures from defect ensembles in a series of cBN samples and find an over- all consistency with previously reported measurements from defect ensembles in hBN.

evidence_result.content: The study finds cBN defect-ensemble ODMR consistent with prior hBN ensemble measurements.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In this work, we study ODMR signatures from defect ensembles in a series of cBN samples and find an over- all consistency with previously reported measurements from defect ensembles in hBN.

evidence_result.content: The large cBN crystal shows weak PL across the sample with occasional brighter spots under 532 nm excitation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Under 532 nm, excitation a weak photoluminescence (PL) signal is consistently ob- served across the sample, as are occasional locations of higher intensity [Fig. 1(c)].

evidence_result.content: PL spectrum shows a broad peak near 700 nm and Raman features at 565 and 573 nm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A PL spectrum taken from a region of the crystal including one of these bright spots yields a large peak centred at approximately 700 nm, with sharp, lower intensity features at 565 nm (1103 cm−1) and 573 nm (1352 cm−1) [Fig. 1(d)].

evidence_result.content: ODMR from a bright cBN region shows a single resonance with about 0.05% contrast at the free-electron Zeeman frequency.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For a select bright region located in the cBN crystal, the ODMR spectrum reveals a single resonance peak with 0.05% contrast at fr ≈gµBB0/h

evidence_result.content: The resonance follows g≈2 when magnetic field is varied.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The g ≈2 scaling is confirmed by measuring the resonant frequency fr while varying the strength of the applied magnetic field, which was calibrated using a hBN sam- ple as a reference [Fig. 1(f)].

evidence_result.content: Both PL and ODMR spectra resemble those previously measured for optical spin defect pairs in hBN.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Both the PL and ODMR spectra bear resemblance to similar measurements of op- tical spin defect pairs in hBN samples.

evidence_result.content: ODMR does not consistently track optical brightness and appears sporadically in both bright and dim regions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Additionally, we note there is no consistent correlation between the opti- cally bright regions and ODMR signal. Instead ODMR is measured sporadically throughout the cBN sample in both bright and dim regions.

evidence_result.content: In 50 µm particles, PL varies strongly between grains and some grains show no PL.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the 50 µm particles, we find the PL intensity of individual grains varies considerably, including some that exhibit no PL response.

evidence_result.content: Unlike the large crystal, PL-active particles show generally uniform PL throughout each grain.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Unlike the large crystal shown in Fig. 1, the PL active particles show generally uniform PL through- out the entire grain of cBN.

evidence_result.content: Smaller grains have weaker but more uniform PL with occasional bright spots.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The two smaller grain sizes show less intense, but more uniform PL across the aggre- gated particles with occasional bright spots distributed throughout.

evidence_result.content: PL spectra for all three samples under 405, 532, and 671 nm excitation show a single broad peak.
evidence_result.evidence_span: PL spectra are measured for the three samples with 405 nm, 532 nm and 671 nm ex- citation and in all cases a single broad peak is observed

evidence_result.content: For 2 µm particles, 405 and 532 nm excitation both produce PL peaking at 700 nm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The only exception is for the 2 µm particles where the PL from both the 405 nm and 532 nm excita- tion lasers peak at 700 nm

evidence_result.content: A resonance was observed in nearly all excitation/sample cases except the 165 nm powder under 671 nm illumination.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Aside from the 165 nm grain sized powder under 671 nm illumination, a resonance was observed in all cases

evidence_result.content: At low microwave powers, a low-amplitude Rabi oscillation is observed and becomes stronger with increasing power.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At lower MW powers, a low amplitude oscillation is observed which becomes more pronounced as the power is increased

evidence_result.content: The Rabi curves are well fit by a two-frequency function with the second frequency fixed at twice the first.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find the Rabi curves are well fit by a two frequency function with frequencies Ω1 and Ω2, where Ω2 is fixed by the relation Ω2 = 2Ω1

evidence_result.content: The Rabi oscillations show an asymmetric envelope at all driving powers.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Furthermore, at all driving powers the Rabi oscillations follow an asymmetric envelope

evidence_result.content: Monoexponential fitting gives an effective spin lifetime of about 3 microseconds.
evidence_result.evidence_span: By fitting the normalised re- laxation curve with a monoexponential function we find T eff 1 ≈3 µs

evidence_result.content: Hahn echo measurements give T2 of about 60 ns.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Fitting the resultant decay curve [Fig. 3(f)] again with a monoexponential function we find T2 ≈60 ns.

evidence_result.content: PL rises immediately then decays to steady state with a settling time of about 260 microseconds.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The PL immediately increases to a maximum value before decaying to a steady state with a 1/e settling time Tsett ≈260 µs

evidence_result.content: PL overshoot recovers with dark time and has a 1/e recovery time of about 3 ms.
evidence_result.evidence_span: plotting the value of the PL overshoot (F/B, integrated over 5 µs of the pulse) as a function of τ shows a clear recovery of the PL, with a 1/e time Trec ≈3 ms as the system is left in the dark for longer periods

evidence_result.content: Confocal and AFM imaging show only a small number of particles in a given field of view.
evidence_result.evidence_span: On each sample, for a given field of view we observe a small number of particles.

evidence_result.content: PL maps alone cannot distinguish single cBN particles from small aggregates.
evidence_result.evidence_span: From the PL maps, we are not able to distinguish single cBN particles from small aggregates

evidence_result.content: AFM shows a well-defined particle in the 2 µm sample but the 165 nm region is more consistent with an aggregate.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the 2 µm sample we are able to measure a well-defined parti- cle, while on the other hand for the 165 nm sample, the selected region appears to be more consistent with a par- ticle aggregate.

evidence_result.content: The 2 µm particle has a plate-like shape with 300 nm height and 2–3 µm lateral size.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Linecuts across the particle/aggregate, shown in Fig. 4(g), reveal the particle from the 2 µm sample has a plate-like shape, as exemplified in Fig. 4(e), where the particle height is 300 nm and the lateral size is 2-3 µm.

evidence_result.content: AFM on isolated regions shows a well-defined particle in the 2 µm sample, while the 165 nm sample appears aggregated.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the 2 µm sample we are able to measure a well-defined parti- cle, while on the other hand for the 165 nm sample, the selected region appears to be more consistent with a par- ticle aggregate.

evidence_result.content: The 2 µm particle is plate-like with 300 nm height and 2–3 µm lateral size.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Linecuts across the particle/aggregate, shown in Fig. 4(g), reveal the particle from the 2 µm sample has a plate-like shape, as exemplified in Fig. 4(e), where the particle height is 300 nm and the lateral size is 2-3 µm.

evidence_result.content: The aggregate height is about 100 nm, suggesting thin plate-like particles.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The maximum height of the aggregate is ∼100 nm which also suggests plate-like particles with a thickness less than the average size, similar to nanodi- amonds [36].

evidence_result.content: SEM images are consistent with the AFM-based morphology picture.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This picture is also consistent with SEM images (see SI).

evidence_result.content: A single 2 µm particle shows ODMR with contrast and linewidth similar to powder films.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The contrast and linewidth from the single particle are consistent with the ODMR measurement from the powder films in Fig. 3

evidence_result.content: In cBN, the ODMR shows a single resonance under magnetic field with spin-1/2-like field scaling over many excitation wavelengths.
evidence_result.evidence_span: notably a single ODMR resonance when under an applied magnetic field with spin-1/2-like scaling with magnetic field strength, which is observable under a wide range of excitation wave- lengths.

evidence_result.content: All samples except the 165 nm one show characteristic cBN Raman TO and LO peaks at 1054 and 1306 cm−1.
evidence_result.evidence_span: All samples except for the 165 nm show distinctive TO and LO peaks at 1054 cm−1 and 1306 cm−1 respectively.

evidence_result.content: The Raman peak positions agree with separate measurements in the main text.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These values are commensu- rate with the separate measurements performed in main text Fig. 1(d)

evidence_result.content: XRD shows identical spectra for all samples, representative of the cBN lattice.
evidence_result.evidence_span: All samples exhibit identical spectra representative of the cBN lattice.

evidence_result.content: FESEM shows the powders are plate-like and confirms average particle sizes.

evidence_result.evidence_span: The observed shapes and sizes are also in agreement with the AFM data in main text Fig. 4.

evidence_result.content: Both constrained and unconstrained versions of the model fit the data well.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For both cases the data is well fit by the model

evidence_result.evidence_span: Fitted Rabi frequency component (Ω1), with linear fit to the components.

constraint.content: The micropowder samples were untreated, i.e., not subject to additional processing such as irradiation or annealing.
evidence_spans: we investigate three different commercially available samples of un- treated (e.g. not subject to additional processing such as irradiation or annealing) micropowders

constraint.content: The relaxation sequence provides only an effective spin lifetime (T1,eff), not a pure T1, because the metastable configuration inferred from the Rabi measurements is convoluted with additional spin-lattice and electronic relaxation processes.
evidence_spans: While this sequence is generally used to measure the longitudinal spin relaxation time T1, the metastable configuration inferred from the Rabi measurements implies convolution with additional processes. As such, only an effective spin life- time T eff 1 can be inferred, accounting for both spin-lattice and electronic relaxation.

constraint.content: Obtaining isolated ODMR measurements on a single 165 nm particle is constrained by aggregation; preventing this would require better understanding of the cBN surface chemistry.
evidence_spans: Taking an ODMR measurement from an isolated single 165 nm particle would require further understanding of the cBN surface chemistry in order to prevent aggrega- tion.
